subtype: Failing an exam and feeling finished [Actor]
passage:
Dear Nilesh,
The result came on Thursday. I failed maths, the one paper everybody expected me to top. In the kitchen Papa went silent and Mummy cried without a sound. Half our building knows by now. I keep thinking my whole plan is finished and I have made everyone ashamed. I know that is probably not how things really are, but tonight it feels that way. This afternoon our class teacher, Kavita ma'am, phoned home and asked us to see the school counsellor together on Monday. Mummy said yes at once. I am writing to you because you failed once too, and I want to know how it got better.
Simran

qa.q: What was Simran feeling on Thursday night?
qa.a: Ashamed and hopeless, feeling the whole plan was finished, though Simran suspects it may not be as permanent as it feels.

qa.q: What step did the class teacher take the same day?
qa.a: Kavita ma'am phoned home and asked Simran and family to see the school counsellor together on Monday.

qa.q: How did Simran's Mummy react to the counsellor idea?
qa.a: Mummy said yes at once, showing support and taking it seriously.

grounding: Shows a teenager who failed a major exam feeling the future has collapsed, with a teacher and family responding the same day.

subtype: Failing an exam and feeling finished [Actor]
passage: Gautam, you want to hear about the time I failed the board exam? Fine. I'm Jeevan. It was Class 10, physics. On result day I stared at the screen and thought that was it: no college, no future, everyone in the neighbourhood talking. I shut myself in my room. That same evening my uncle knocked, sat on the bed with two cups of tea and said nothing about marks. Then he said, "Tomorrow morning we'll talk to the school counsellor." We went. The counsellor listened and said that the feeling of "this is permanent" is common after a shock, and we planned the supplementary exam together. I still remember how heavy it was, and how it lifted a little.

qa.q: Which subject did Jeevan fail in Class 10?
What did Jeevan feel on result day?
qa.a: Hopeless and ashamed, thinking that was the end of college and any future.
The uncle sat quietly with tea that same evening and took Jeevan to the school counsellor the next morning.

qa.q: How might the uncle have seen Jeevan's situation?
qa.a: With concern and care, choosing not to start with marks and acting the same evening.

grounding: Shows a teenager who failed a board exam feeling everything has collapsed, and a family member helping the same day.
